trail: Wikiquote’s sourced section ↗ for Awaken the Giant Within (1992) prints this sentence and cites page 49. We read the page’s raw wikitext rather than a summary, so the wording and the page number are as Wikiquote states them.

The edition history checks out independently: the Internet Archive catalogue record ↗ gives “New York: Simon & Schuster, 1992,” 552 pages, 1st Fireside edition, and notes that it was “originally published: New York : Summit Books, c1991” — which is why this page dates the work to 1991 and the pagination to 1992.

Limit of what we checked: the page location rests on Wikiquote’s citation. The Internet Archive copy is lending-restricted and Google Books returned a bot challenge, so we did not confirm page 49 against the book’s own text.
source.excerptNote: Wikiquote prints the pair of sentences together. The second one is the test the first is talking about, and it is usually dropped when the line is reshared.

author.bio: Tony Robbins, born Anthony J. Mahavoric in 1960, built the modern self-help seminar into an industry. Unlimited Power (1986) made his name and Awaken the Giant Within (1991) became the book most often quoted from, usually one sentence at a time. The lines that circulate from it are typically the opening sentence of a longer paragraph, which is why so many Robbins quotations are genuine but truncated.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The sentence is doing a definitional job in the book: Robbins is distinguishing a decision from an intention, and the measure he offers is behavioural rather than emotional.
Quoted on its own it reads as an aphorism. With the following sentence attached — “If there’s no action, you haven’t truly decided” — it reads as a definition, which is what it is.
detailsBody: Awaken the Giant Within is a 1991 book of about 550 pages, and the lines quoted from it are almost always single sentences lifted from the start of a paragraph. That is worth knowing before trusting any short Robbins quotation: the attribution is usually fine, and the sentence is usually only part of what he wrote.
context.pull: No action, no decision — that is the whole test.
